request.spec:
The screen gains a header with counters, shown at all times: the number of people on the sheet
(retired people included), the number of claims in each status (DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING, SETTLED,
VOID), the sheet's due-total and the sheet's overdue-total. Each counter always equals the figure
it repeats: the status counts those of the summary, the two totals the sheet's totals.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The screen gains a header with counters, shown at all times: the number of people on the sheet
(retired people included), the number of claims in each status (DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING, SETTLED,
VOID), the sheet's due-total and the sheet's overdue-total. Each counter always equals the figure
it repeats: the status counts those of the summary, the two totals the sheet's totals.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The sheet now has a header with the counters, and all 4 acceptance tests pass under `bin/e2e`.

It shows the number of people on the sheet (retired people included), the number of claims in each status (DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING, SETTLED, VOID), the due-total and the overdue-total. It sits at the top of the sheet's panels, so you see it whenever a sheet is loaded. Before a sheet is loaded there are no figures to show, so it doesn't appear then.

To keep each counter equal to the figure it repeats, the header works its numbers out with the same code as the screens that already show them:
- **Totals:** I moved the calculation that was inside the totals panel (`rollup.slot.tsx`) into a shared hook, `features/claims/useSheetTotals.ts`. That panel and the header both use it now.
- **Status counts:** I moved the list of statuses into `features/claims/useClaims.ts`, next to the claim status type. The summary and the header both use it and count claims the same way.

The header itself is in `features/header/header.slot.tsx`. Only the front end changed; the server and stored data didn't need anything, and the request adds no audit records.
